leads.name: Oaks and lime of January 13
leads.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-26, delivered as sll_002 in data/cities/silale.json
leads.species: Oak (Quercus sp., x13) and Lime (Tilia sp., x1)
leads.species_basis: genus read from lt.wikipedia's description of the grove; individual species per tree not itemised in the source
leads.reason: Checked 2026-09-06, held as a lead. NOT the same monument as the neighbouring 'Šilalė Independence oak' (see that entry, about 90m away), and NOT folded into one entry with it: this is a distinct memorial grove of 13 oaks and 1 linden, planted in a semicircle around the 'Laisvės šauklys' (Freedom's Crier) sculpture by Kazimieras Kisielis, at the same J. Basanavičiaus / Nepriklausomybės street intersection in central Šilalė. lt.wikipedia (Sausio 13-osios ąžuolai ir liepa) plus a second, independent source (pamatyklietuvoje.lt and silalesbiblioteka.lt both describe the monument) confirm: the 13 oaks + 1 linden represent the 13 men and 1 woman killed defending Lithuanian freedom on 13 January 1991 (the Vilnius TV-tower/Freedom Defenders' Day attack). Sources differ on which anniversary the monument itself marks, so both facts are recorded rather than merged into one claim: one source calls the sculpture Lithuania's first monument to 11 March 1990 (Restoration of Independence), an idea from 1990 realised in 1998. Declared a municipal natural heritage object in 2006, protected area 0.21ha, in a roughly triangular plot with benches, bounded by two streets and adjacent buildings ('intense automobile movement' nearby, per the register). No individual girth, height or planting date recorded for the trees themselves; likely planted around 1990-1998 alongside the monument, so young (roughly 30-35 years) rather than ancient, with the case resting on historical significance rather than age or size. Reads as one compact, collectible ensemble, a semicircle around one monument with one obvious place to stand, not an avenue or a wood. Access: public street-corner plot, no gate or fee, genuinely reachable. A fuller municipal list of Šilalė's protected objects may hold more (silale.lt/kaimo-reikalai-ir-aplinkos-apsauga/savivaldybes-saugomu-gamtos-paveldo-objektu-sarasas/) but the whole site Cloudflare-blocks automated fetches (two attempts, WebFetch and curl with a spoofed user agent, both refused, not a hang; worth adding to data/fetch-blocklist.json and worth a browser-session check on a future pass). VERIFIED 2026-09-26: even combined with the neighbouring Independence Oak, Šilalė town centre alone still has only these 2 collectible points, short of the 4-tree floor on its own; but paired with two out-of-town finds from this same pass (Laumenai Oak and Pundžiai Oak, both in the Kaltinėnai area of the same Šilalė district), the four together clear the floor as a proposed new city. See data/research/_famous-lithuania-verified.json for the full 4-tree Šilalė cluster writeup (sll_001 through sll_004); this entry is sll_002. NOTE: this exact lead (same name, coordinates and photos) appears TWICE in this file; both occurrences have been updated identically, they are the same tree, not two.

leads.name: Gelgaudiškis manor park oaks
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.reason: Checked in depth 2026-09-07: this is a real cluster inside the 118 ha Gelgaudiskis manor park (a national landscape-monument park since 2001), but it lands short in both directions the task asked about. lt.wikipedia's own park article names five individually designated gamtos paveldo objektai here: 'pirmasis azuolas' (I), 'antrasis azuolas' (II), 'III azuolas', 'IV azuolas' and a pine ('Gelgaudiskio pusis'), all within about 700 m of each other, easily walkable. Checked each one's own lt.wikipedia page individually (the register carries no vitality field, so this is always our own check): the IV oak's own article says plainly '2023 m. duomenimis, azuolas buvo nudziuves, be zieves ... Paskelbtas sunykusiu' (as of 2023 it was dried out, without bark, officially declared decayed) and the pine's article likewise says it is 'nudziuvusi, beveik be zieves' with a 2019 assessment calling it rotting and 'likely to fall soon.' Both are BLOCKED as dead, leaving only THREE confirmed-alive designated oaks: I (Quercus robur, girth 4.70 m, height 27-28 m, age ~300 years per the state register and the State Forest Service's own 'Senieji Lietuvos azuolai' survey no. 82, healthy, described as 'storiausias is dvaro parko azuolu', the thickest of the park's oaks), II (girth 3.92 m, height 29 m, age ~200 years, same two sources, largely healthy though a 2021 official quality review recommended demoting it to the municipal list as a lesser specimen), and III (girth 3.8 m, height 25 m, municipally designated 2004, no age given, species not restated in its own article beyond the shared genus). Three does not clear the ordinary 4-tree floor for a walkable multi-tree place. None of the three individually clears the 2026-08-31 single-tree destination bar either on current evidence: all are undistinguished protected oaks of a size and age comparable to already-held leads (Latezeris oak 4.35 m/held, Bagrenas linden 5.45 m/held), with no record claim, award or named legend found, unlike the park's formerly famous spruce (Gelgaudiskio egle, once the thickest and tallest in Suvalkija) which itself died and was felled before 2010. leads.name: Šilalė Independence oak
leads.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-26, delivered as sll_001 in data/cities/silale.json
leads.species_basis: confirmed by lt.wikipedia infobox (paprastasis ąžuolas)
leads.reason: Checked 2026-09-06, held as a lead at the time. NOT the same monument as the neighbouring 'Oaks and lime of January 13' grove (see that entry, about 90m away): this is one older single oak on a traffic island at the J. Basanavičiaus / Nepriklausomybės street intersection in central Šilalė. lt.wikipedia (Nepriklausomybės ąžuolas) gives height 15.0m, girth 2.40m at 1.3m, age 94 years as of 2022 (roughly 98 now); stone markers at its base read '1918-02-16' (Lithuania's independence day). Planting date is disputed between sources rather than resolved: one historian (Kazimieras Šetkus) says planted by the Šilalė riflemen's association in autumn 1937 for the 20th independence anniversary; another account gives 1927-28 for the 10th anniversary, organised by pharmacist Simonas Gaudėšius and municipal officials; a bottle with a written testament was reportedly buried under it, recovery status unknown. Declared a municipal natural heritage object in 2006. Two sources found: lt.wikipedia (drawing on the register) and the dated 2023 Commons photo record; an independent news source specifically about this tree was not located. Alive and actively tended: since 2018 the municipality has run restoration work (soil remediation, mulching, wire removal, winter salt protection) because the tree is damaged by passing trucks and road salt at the intersection, which is itself evidence of recent continued life. Access: public street island, no gate or fee, genuinely reachable, though it stands amid busy traffic. At 2.40m girth it is not an exceptional specimen by Lithuanian standards, and its fame is local rather than national, so it does not clearly clear the 2026-08-31 single-tree destination bar ALONE. A fuller municipal list of Šilalė's protected objects may hold more (silale.lt/kaimo-reikalai-ir-aplinkos-apsauga/savivaldybes-saugomu-gamtos-paveldo-objektu-sarasas/) but the whole site Cloudflare-blocks automated fetches (two attempts, WebFetch and curl with a spoofed user agent, both refused, not a hang; worth adding to data/fetch-blocklist.json and worth a browser-session check on a future pass). VERIFIED 2026-09-26: combined with the neighbouring January 13 grove PLUS two new out-of-town finds from this same pass, Laumenai Oak and Pundžiai Oak (both in the Kaltinėnai area of the same Šilalė district, ~16-18km out and ~6.5km from each other), these four together clear the ordinary 4-tree floor as a proposed new city, two walkable town points plus two car-reachable countryside stops, the same shape as several other cities in this file. RECOMMEND a future write pass open Šilalė as a new city (data/cities/silale.json does not yet exist) with these four as sll_001 through sll_004; this entry as sll_001, the anchor. See data/research/_famous-lithuania-verified.json for the full cluster writeup.
